key_claims: Power-to-weight ratio above 6.5 watts per kilogram is required for Grand Tour GC riders to compete on long alpine climbs
Classics riders are typically 70+ kg with higher absolute power but lower power-to-weight ratio, making them suited for flat roads where power and CDA are primary determinants
Training Stress Score (TSS) is calculated as a function of one-hour maximum effort; riding at full gas for one hour = 100 TSS, while 50% intensity for two hours also equals 100 TSS
Grand Tour peaking requires lower fitness in April compared to classics riders targeting Tour of Flanders, with fitness mapped over 42-day running totals
Wout Van Aert is the best rider on the planet because he can compete in Grand Tours, climb alpine passes three weeks into races, perform time trials on flats, and race cyclocross in winter
specific_numbers: 6.5-6.57 watts per kilogram power-to-weight ratio for GC riders
TSS 100 for full gas one hour effort
